The '''Hiemuekan Desert''' is a large, [[wikipedia:Desert_climate#Cold_desert_climates|cold desert]] and [[wikipedia:/Grassland|grassland]] region in Kaastini and in western and southern [[Dahe]], It is the -----largest desert in the world.

The name of the desert comes from the [[Kaastini language|Kaastini]] word Hiemu, used to refer to all of the waterless regions in the [[Kaastini Plateau]]; in [[Dahen Language|Dahen]], Hiemu is used to refer to cold, waterless areas such as the Hiemuekan itself rather than sandy deserts.

== Geography ==
The Hiemuekan Desert is widest in the south. Its area is approximately 735,400 square kilometres (456,956 sq mi). Hiemuekan includes the long stretch of desert extending from the foot of the [[Omoso]] and [[Kozhika Mountains]]; and from the foothills of the [[Chuanyi]], on the west and north, it surrounds the [[Aeses River basin]].

Some geographers and ecologists prefer to regard the northeastern area of the Hiemuekan desert (as defined above): a distinct and separate desert called the [[Machiis desert]].

Much of the Hiemuekan is not sandy, instead resembling exposed bare rock or grasslands.

== Climate ==
The Hiemuekan is overall a [[wikipedia:Desert_climate#Cold_desert_climates|cold desert]], with frost and occasionally snow occurring on its dunes. Besides being quite far north, it is also located in an area roughly 400–1000 m  above sea level, which contributes to its low temperatures. An average of about 194 mm (7.6 in) of rain falls annually in the Hiemuekan. Additional moisture reaches parts of the Hiemuekan in winter.  Winds may cause the Hiemuekan to reach −40 °C (−40 °F) in winter to 45 °C (113 °F) in summer.

However, the climate of the Hiemuekan is one of great extremes, with rapid changes of [[wikipedia:Temperature|temperature]] of as much as 35 °C (63 °F) in 24-hour spans. 
===Desertification===
The Hiemuekan Desert is expanding through [[wikipedia:Desertification|desertification]], most rapidly on the eastern edge into [[Dahe]], which is seeing 3,600 km2 (1,390 sq mi) of [[wikipedia:Grassland|grassland]] overtaken every year. [[wikipedia:Dust_storm|Dust storms]] increased in frequency between 1750 and 1760, causing further damage to [[Dahen agriculture economy|Dahes's agriculture economy]]. However, in some areas, desertification has been slowed or reversed.

The northern and eastern boundaries between desert and grassland are constantly changing. This is mostly due to the climate conditions before the growing season, which influence the rate of evapotranspiration and subsequent plant growth.

The expansion of the Hiemuekan is attributed mostly to [[Human activities in the Hiemuekan desert|human activities]], locally driven by [[wikipedia:deforestation|deforestation]], overgrazing, and depletion of water resources, as well as to [wikipedia:Climate_change|climate change]].

[[Dahe]] has tried various plans to slow the expansion of the desert, which have met with some success. The [[Dahen government]] has implemented a tree-planting project begun in 1732 and set to continue through to 1800. The goal of the program is to [[wikipedia:Desertification#Reversing_desertification|reverse desertification]] by planting aspen and other fast-growing trees.
